name: maennchen1 Newsletter Germany
author: maennchen1.de

sections.description:
maennchen1 Newsletter Germany turns WordPress into a newsletter system. Subscribers live in tables of
your own WordPress database, and mail is sent over the mail path of your own server. No
subscriber address and no sending statistic is handed to a third party, because there is no
third party involved.

The plugin was written for German and European operators, where data protection law makes
the location of subscriber data a practical question rather than a preference.

What it does

  • A subscription form for your site, as a block, a shortcode or a widget
  • Double opt-in, with a confirmation mail the operator writes
  • An unsubscribe link in every mail: one click, no login (or confirmed by mail, if you prefer)
  • Subscriber groups, so one newsletter can go to a chosen audience
  • Newsletters in HTML and plain text, sent as multipart mail
  • Scheduled sending over WP-Cron, in batches sized for shared hosting
  • An archive page and a browser view for readers whose mail client mangles HTML
  • Placeholders such as %abo_vorname% anywhere in subject and body
  • Layout templates, and your own templates in an upload folder that updates never touch

Optional modules

Each of these is a separate file that can be switched on in the backend and left off
otherwise:

  • A sending log of who received which newsletter
  • Placeholder rules, for example for salutations
  • Post notification, immediately or collected as a daily or weekly summary
  • Spam protection for the subscription and unsubscription form, without a puzzle, without a
    third party and without storing an IP address

Requirements

PHP 8.1 or newer with the extensions dom and simplexml. A working mail path on the server —
either PHP mail, an SMTP account or wp_mail.

External services

This plugin contacts no server of the manufacturer and no third-party service. Mail goes
out over the mail path of your own server, and no subscriber data leaves your
installation.

One setting fetches content from elsewhere: with “Embed images in the mail” switched on, the
plugin downloads every image used in a newsletter from the address it is hosted at (usually
your own site) and attaches it to the mail. Nothing is sent along except the request for the
image. The setting is off by default.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins > Add New > Upload, or unpack the ZIP into
    wp-content/plugins
  2. Activate it in the plugin list. The database tables are created on activation
  3. Open Newsletter > Configuration and set the sender address and the mail path
  4. Create at least one group under Newsletter > Groups. Subscribers are assigned to groups
  5. Open Newsletter > Configuration > Page configuration and choose “Create and assign new”
    for the subscription, confirmation, unsubscribe and archive pages, then save. Until
    these pages exist, the backend shows a notice that names the missing ones
  6. Place the subscription form on your site: insert the block “Newsletter form”,
    write the shortcode [wpng_form] into a page, or use the widget
sections.faq:
Where is the subscriber data stored?

In tables of your own WordPress database, prefixed with the prefix of your installation.
Nothing is sent to the manufacturer or to any other service.

Which mail path is used?

Whichever you configure: the internal PHP mail function, an SMTP account, or wp_mail so that
an existing SMTP plugin handles delivery. Deliverability depends on that path — SPF, DKIM
and DMARC are set up at your host, not in this plugin.

Are IP addresses of subscribers stored?

No. Neither IP addresses nor user agents are recorded.

Can a subscriber be deleted completely?

Yes. Deleting a subscriber also deletes their group assignments and their sending records.

Does the plugin work with the privacy tools of WordPress?

Yes. Under Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data, enter a mail
address and the plugin answers: the subscriber record, groups, and which newsletters were
sent and when. Erasing removes all of it. Settings > Privacy offers a suggested text for
your privacy policy.

What happens to the data when the plugin is deleted?

Nothing, unless you say so. By default subscribers, newsletters and settings survive the
deletion of the plugin, so that removing it by accident costs nothing. Under Settings >
Maintenance you can switch this: with the setting on, deleting the plugin removes all
tables, all settings including stored passwords, the upload folder and the cron entry.
The pages the plugin created for subscription, confirmation, unsubscribe and archive are
always kept — they may carry your own text.

Does sending survive a short PHP time limit?

Yes. Sending runs in batches over WP-Cron, and the batch size is configurable. The default
is sized for shared hosting with a 30 second limit.

Is there a free and a paid edition?

Yes. This plugin is the free edition and complete in itself: nothing in it is locked, limited
in time or waiting for a key. The manufacturer sells a paid edition with further modules
separately, outside this directory.
sections.changelog:
The full history is in the file changelog.txt inside the plugin folder.

2.0.2

  • Changed: translations — every text can now be translated on translate.wordpress.org

2.0.1

  • Security: backend — settings only save when the form is submitted
  • Security: content — saved filtered without “unfiltered_html”
  • Security: output — escaped throughout
  • Security: settings backup — could create PHP objects when loaded
  • Added: cron — own address with a key
  • Changed: loading — styles and scripts only where needed
  • Changed: name — the plugin is now called “maennchen1 Newsletter Germany”
  • Changed: page lists — newsletter pages no longer in automatic page lists
  • Changed: post notification — “Zusammenfassung” instead of “Digest” in German
  • Changed: requirements — WordPress 6.2 or later
  • Changed: sign-up — no longer reveals whether an address is on the list
  • Changed: unsubscribe — one click on new installations
  • Fixed: directories — files not found when the content folder was moved
  • Fixed: general — many smaller bugs
  • Fixed: mail — “HTML and text mail” sent only HTML
  • Fixed: MySQL 8 — newsletter table missing, CSV export failed
  • Fixed: newsletters and delivery log — paging through the list did not work
  • Fixed: sender — sender address lost after saving
  • Fixed: subject — placeholders lost
  • Fixed: unsubscribe — signing up again was impossible
  • Fixed: widget — did not appear

2.0.0

  • Security: browser view — no longer hands out other subscribers’ newsletters
  • Security: confirmation and unsubscribe links — much stronger token
  • Security: CSV export — names no longer run as formulas
  • Security: database errors — no backtrace with subscriber data
  • Security: menu icon — no request to the manufacturer
  • Security: text version — could run code from the address bar
  • Security: unsubscribe form — no longer reveals whether an address is on the list
  • Added: defaults — a new installation works from the first screen
  • Added: help — every admin page links to the manual
  • Added: maintenance — new area to clean up existing data
  • Added: panels — collapsible on the newsletter, subscriber and group screens
  • Added: placeholders — %nl_onlineurl% and %nl_onlinelink%
  • Added: privacy — WordPress privacy tools supported
  • Added: spam protection — new module without puzzle or third-party service
  • Added: target group — shows how many subscribers are reached
  • Added: uninstall — optional removal of all data
  • Changed: admin — configuration area and screens refreshed
  • Changed: help — manual in the language of the backend
  • Changed: mail engine — “MIME mailer” removed, WP mailer instead
  • Changed: menu — “Mailkonfiguration” is now “Absender und Betreff”
  • Changed: session — no PHP session and no cookie for visitors
  • Removed: CKEditor and old bundled libraries
  • Removed: downloading executable archives at runtime
  • Fixed: browser view — link led to “invalid subscriber”
  • Fixed: general — many smaller bugs and accessibility
  • Fixed: images in mails — wrong type, embedding ignored
  • Fixed: inline editing — did not save
  • Fixed: scripts and styles — stale after a plugin update
  • Fixed: sending run — scheduled several times instead of once
  • Fixed: subscriber deletion — sending records left behind
  • Fixed: time zone — date placeholders and scheduled sending
  • Fixed: update by hand — database updates itself
